newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Confidence returns to copper market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Confidence returns to copper market.

text.p: The copper market ended the week on a buoyant note and helped to instil a more confident tone to some of the other base metals.
In soft commodities cocoa managed to record further gains but looked to be losing some of its sharp upward momentum while the coffee market came in for another bout of selling.
London Metal Exchange (LME) copper received an early boost from news that stocks in warehouses linked to the LME had fallen by 4,275 tonnes.
This helped to take the market well clear of a technical support level just above $2,300 which had been under threat earlier in the week and encouraged some speculative buying and shortcovering.
"It's looking good again, its starting to turn round. We may see it head back to test the $2,375 resistance,' analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
Copper ended the Friday at $2,356, up $17 a tonne from Thursday.
LME zinc prices, no longer being held back by an uncertain copper market, soared to fresh 4-1/2 year highs when metal for three months delivery reached $1,292 a tonne.

There was a feeling in the cocoa market that prices may have seen the top for the time being and this brought out a fair amount of profit-taking and made the fund's rather cautious about adding to their long positions.
Analysts said there was no change in the supply scenario with the world cocoa market expected to be in a production deficit, but this had probably now been discounted by the past month's gains.

The main question in cocoa would be how large would the deficit be and this would depend mainly on the size of the Ivory Coast crop where figures from officials and analysts vary considerably mostly over a 200,000 tonnes range arounde one million tonnes.
Cocoa still moved higher on the day but ended below its best levels.

Coffee dropped more than $50 a tonne at one stage the feeling spread that the market was due for a pause in this year's sharp run-up in prices. But roaster buying helped to stabilise prices and restore confidence and by the close losses had been trimmed.
Precious metals were mostly stable with gold eyeing developments in New York where March options expire on Friday and palladium traders still waiting for news as to when Russia wil resume exports.
